title: MorphoEval: Scoring the Faithfulness of Morphology Reproductions and Publishing the Scores as Nanopublications
description:
This deposition bundles the MorphoEval Reproducibility Report — a preprint that explains how the MorphoEval evaluation layer works and presents its audits of the morphology reproductions in the morpholib repository — together with the complete source code of the repository at the corresponding revision. Two files are included: the report PDF and a full archive of the source.

MorphoEval is a seven-dimension, weighted rubric (model fidelity, specimen match, parameter expressivity, morphometric validation, source traceability, code traceability, reproducibility package) applied to Python reproductions of published models of biological form: Thompson's coordinate transformations (1917), Gray–Scott/Turing patterns, Raup's shell-coiling morphospace, the Planform and Limbform graph-encoded morphologies (Lobo & Levin), the WormGUIDES C. elegans embryo atlas, the Hoffmann–Donoughe insect wing-venation model, Odonata wing cells in fossils, and a direct test of Thompson's Scarus → Pomacanthus transformation on 791 real species. Every score is backed by line-pinned evidence at a recorded commit and by measurements taken on the rendered outputs, and every audit is published as ProbKnow-template-conformant nanopublications (one pk:LLMClaimAssessment per dimension plus an overall verdict), signed, independently verified, and placed on the production nanopublication network, where re-scores supersede earlier ones.

MorphoEval is the simulation-faithfulness sibling of BioEval (10.5281/zenodo.20567719) and NeuroEval (10.5281/zenodo.20622878). All scores to date come from a single LLM assessor that also wrote most of the audited code; the knowledge graph is designed so that further assessors can add their own assessments of the same hypotheses.
